[Issue #9081] Update and validate custom fields (#9282)

## Summary

<!-- Use "Fixes" to automatically close issue upon PR merge. Use "Work
for" when UAT is required. -->
Fixes #9081  

## Changes proposed

<!-- What was added, updated, or removed in this PR. -->

- Added typed Pydantic schemas for each CommonGrants custom field in a
new common_grants_pydantic_custom_fields.py module
- Added a validate_custom_field() helper function in transformation.py
that validates custom field data against its typed Pydantic schema
before including it in the response
- Updated populate_custom_fields() to use the new typed field classes
and validate_custom_field() instead of constructing generic CustomField
instances directly
- Tightened Marshmallow schema field types in
common_grants_custom_fields.py — replacing fields.Raw() with typed
alternatives (fields.Integer, fields.String, fields.Boolean,
  fields.Nested, fields.List)
- Reorganized schemas into a schemas/ subdirectory
(common_grants_custom_fields.py and common_grants_schemas.py moved under
schemas/)
- Updated imports in common_grants_routes.py to reflect the new module
paths

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the
implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about
that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->

Previously, populate_custom_fields() constructed all custom fields using
the generic CustomField base class with untyped value fields, meaning
invalid data could silently pass through
without validation. This PR introduces a typed Pydantic subclass for
each custom field (e.g., LegacySerialIdField, AgencyField,
AttachmentsField) that enforces value types at
  construction time.

The validate_custom_field() wrapper catches validation errors, logs a
warning with the OPPORTUNITY_VALIDATION_ERROR event, and returns None so
the caller can skip including invalid
fields in the response rather than crashing or silently serving bad
data.

The AttachmentValue model also includes special handling for
downloadUrl: it attempts to parse the value as a valid HttpUrl and falls
back to None if it's malformed, rather than
  failing the entire field.

## Validation steps

<!-- Manual testing instructions, as well as any helpful references
(screenshots, GIF demos, code examples or output). -->


Start the common grants endpoints with data

```bash

poetry install

# Start API with data
make init 
make db-seed-local && make populate-search-opportunities
make run-logs
```

Run the following curl commands to validate.


List:

'GET' 'http://localhost:8080/common-grants/opportunities'`

'GET'
'http://localhost:8080/common-grants/opportunities/8b5f468a-8530-4e4f-9d72-a5713adbc0ec'`


Search:
`curl -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'X-Api-Key: two_org_user_key' -X
'POST' 'http://localhost:8080/common-grants/opportunities/search' -d '{
"filters": { "status": { "operator": "in", "value": ["open",
"forecasted"] }, "pagination": { "page": 1, "pageSize": 10 }, "search":
"education", "sorting": { "sortBy": "lastModifiedAt", "sortOrder":
"desc" } }' `

[Issue #9150] Enable OpenSearch Query Explanation Logging (#9289)

## Summary

<!-- Use "Fixes" to automatically close issue upon PR merge. Use "Work
for" when UAT is required. -->
Fixes #9150

## Changes proposed

<!-- What was added, updated, or removed in this PR. -->
Adds `opensearch_explain.py`. Parses OpenSearch _explanation trees into
flat field -> score mappings and emits them as `SearchResultExplanation`
custom events in New Relic for the top 10 results per search.
Added `took_ms` and `raw_hits` fields so the search response carries
both query latency and the raw hit objects (including _explanation)
Added `OPENSEARCH_EXPLAIN_ENABLED` env var (default: true).
Added explain: bool = False parameter to search() — merges {"explain":
True} into the query body when set.
OPENSEARCH_EXPLAIN_ENABLED=true added to environment_variables.tf .

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the
implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about
that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->
When users report poor search results we have no visibility into why
results ranked where they did. This adds OpenSearch explanation logging
to surface per-field scoring breakdowns as New Relic
SearchResultExplanation custom events for the top 10 results per search,
along with search.took_ms instrumentation for latency monitoring.

OPENSEARCH_EXPLAIN_ENABLED (default: true) serves as a kill switch if
explain queries cause latency regressions.

## Validation steps

<!-- Manual testing instructions, as well as any helpful references
(screenshots, GIF demos, code examples or output). -->
See updated unit tests.

head_commit.message: [Issue #8872] Opportunity publish workflow writes to search index (#9300) ## Summary Fixes #8872 ## Changes proposed * In the opportunity publish workflow, write the opportunity to the search index * Adds a workflow client registry for getting the search client when needed in workflow logic ## Context for reviewers The implementation here is slightly different than the ticket. There's no branching logic with conditionals if there isn't a current opportunity summary because adding that would have needed more steps/events as that check would have to happen after we handle setting the opportunity summary in the prior step. So regardless of what we do, the same events would happen, we could add a conditional so it doesn't even go into the new handler function, but an if-statement at the start seems more straightforward / intuitive. Will leave that to the publish folks to sort out in the future if they don't like the history this leaves. In the interest of not needing to plumb more clients through in the future (like an eventual client for integrating our two services with each other) especially when they're only needed for specific workflows - we'll instead have this global registry that we can use in a very similar manner. It might be we want to adjust how it works down the road, but the search client is fine to be shared like this - we initialize one client and share it across all endpoints in the API, so it's well tested. ## Validation steps Make sure your API is running locally. Run `make console` and create an opportunity that won't have a current summary, but will get one. ```py opportunity = f.OpportunityFactory.create(is_draft=True, no_current_summary=True) f.OpportunitySummaryFactory.create(opportunity=opportunity, is_forecast=False) ``` Send an event to the event API using the `internal_workflow_user_key` API key, setting the opportunity ID from what you created above. ```json { "event_type": "start_workflow", "metadata": {}, "start_workflow_context": { "entity_id": "4b1cf004-1034-407b-90ab-9e16c2008ad5", "entity_type": "opportunity", "workflow_type": "opportunity_publish" } } ``` Run the workflow service with: `make cmd args="workflow workflow-main"` - you shouldn't see any errors processing the event. [Issue #9149] Log OpenSearch Relevance and Data Completeness Metrics  (#9294)

## Summary

<!-- Use "Fixes" to automatically close issue upon PR merge. Use "Work
for" when UAT is required. -->
Fixes #9149 

## Changes proposed

<!-- What was added, updated, or removed in this PR. -->
Added max_score, total_relation, scoring_rule, and per-aggregation
agg_overflow to structured request logs for OpenSearch searches.

- max_score and total_relation are parsed from the OpenSearch response
and logged at the adapter
layer via `add_extra_data_to_current_request_logs`, consistent with the
pattern established in #9296
for `took_ms`, `timed_out`, and `shards_failed`.
- `agg_overflow` captures sum_other_doc_count for all aggregations
generically (not just agency),
logged as `search.agg_overflow.<name>`. Non-zero values indicate a facet
is silently truncating
buckets.
- `scoring_rule` is logged at the service layer since it derives from
search params, not the
OpenSearch response.   

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the
implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about
that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->
Beyond the core performance metrics in
https://github.com/HHS/simpler-grants-gov/issues/9147, OpenSearch
returns relevance and data completeness signals that help us monitor
search quality over time. Without these we can't detect scoring
degradation, verify result count accuracy, or know when filter facets
are silently truncating options. Important for ongoing search quality
monitoring as we experiment with scoring changes.

## Validation steps

<!-- Manual testing instructions, as well as any helpful references
(screenshots, GIF demos, code examples or output). -->

Added max_score, total_relation, scoring_rule, and per-aggregation
agg_overflow to structured request logs for OpenSearch searches.

and logged at the adapter
layer via `add_extra_data_to_current_request_logs`, consistent with the
pattern established in #9296
for `took_ms`, `timed_out`, and `shards_failed`.

generically (not just agency),

is silently truncating

search params, not the

returns relevance and data completeness signals that help us monitor
search quality over time. Without these we can't detect scoring
degradation, verify result count accuracy, or know when filter facets
are silently truncating options. Important for ongoing search quality
monitoring as we experiment with scoring changes.
